prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: EN · Plan comparison (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Feature" · longest unbreakable word 56px · one-line width 83px
  col 2: header "Free" · longest unbreakable word 79px · one-line width 79px
  col 3: header "Pro" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 66px
  col 4: header "Enterprise" · longest unbreakable word 75px · one-line width 229px
  col 5: header "Notes" · longest unbreakable word 73px · one-line width 419px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare three plans feature by feature, with a free-text Notes column for caveats and supporting detail.","reading":"Readers scan the Feature column down the rows, then compare Free, Pro and Enterprise across each row; Notes is read secondarily after the plan values and is not part of the main tier comparison.","groups":["Free, Pro and Enterprise are peer plan columns and should read as one comparison block.","Feature is the row-label column and should stay visually distinct from the plan values.","Notes is supplementary commentary, so its width can flex against the plan block."],"keep_intact":["Feature, Free, Pro, Enterprise headers","Community, Unlimited, Custom, 1 year, 30 days, —, ✓","SSO / SAML","24/7"],"may_wrap":["Notes prose","the long Enterprise cell 24/7 phone & dedicated manager","longer Notes such as response-time and Okta/Azure details"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [130, 100, 90, 170, 229] · table 720×335px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 83, 36, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [125, 110, 110, 110, 264] · table 720×335px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60, 36, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [110, 100, 87, 100, 322] · table 720×358px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60, 36, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
